exposure: Completeness of antenatal medical records (admission, history, examination, progress notes, nursing notes, vital signs, procedures, clinical pharmaceutical records)
outcome: Adverse fetal outcomes (prolonged labor, preeclampsia, neonatal distress)
cohort: The study assessed 100 patient files of antenatal obstetric patients, reflecting a diverse range from both low- and high-risk categories, at the IMCH PUMHS Obstetrics & Gynecology Ward, Unit II.
finding: Incomplete antenatal medical record documentation, particularly on admission, vital signs, and pharmaceutical sheets, correlated with adverse maternal and fetal outcomes including prolonged labor, preeclampsia, neonatal distress, NICU admissions, stillbirths, and maternal infections or death.
